brief: A herb planter with soil in its bins that is non-toxic if my cat chews on it.

requirements.evidence: 4 full bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full) each with hex-bin-full bin; planted basil-young x2, parsley-young, thyme-young (props 1-4), visible from above
fillSoil applied to all 4 bins via fill_and_plant; check_build ok, no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL

Parts are 3D-printed in a user-chosen material; configurator checks fit/collisions only and knows nothing about materials, toxicity, or food safety. No material choice here can make the printed plastic guaranteed non-toxic if chewed. Chose basil/parsley/thyme plant props (avoided mint) but that does not make the build itself non-toxic.
requirements.requirement: Non-toxic if cat chews on it

finish.summary: Built a 4-cell herb planter with full bins, each filled with soil and planted with cat-friendly herbs (basil, parsley, thyme). The non-toxic requirement cannot be met by this configurator because toxicity depends on the user-chosen print material, which it does not control.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
